items.title: Refurbished vs New Laptops in India: Which Is the Better Deal in 2026?
items.summary: Every online laptop listing looks compelling until you try to untangle the warranty terms. Refurbished devices often undercut new prices by a meaningful margin, but what you save upfront can disappear quickly if battery capacity fades or after-sales support falls short. This guide walks through what actually separates a sound purchase from a stressful one. Refurbished vs New: How the Real Difference Plays Out The price gap between a refurbished and a new laptop can look significant sometimes, ₹10,000 to ₹20,000 on the same model. But the comparison does not end at the sticker price. What you give up with refurbished: A refurbished laptop has a usage history. That history is invisible to you at the time of purchase. Battery health degrades with charge cycles, and most refurbished listings do not state this clearly. Cosmetic condition grades like "Grade A" or "like new" vary significantly by seller and carry no standardised definition in India. Accessories (charger, documentation, original box) may or may not be included.
